info.title: Avelorn
info.summary: The unit and army database for Warhammer: The Old World.

get.summary: Evaluate the volley program with both sides' rules attached
get.description:
Ten Elven Archers shoot twenty Elven Spearmen at 12 inches.

Each side's rules attach to the steps they reach.

Returns:
    The evaluated volley program.

schema.title: Response Graph Volley Graph Volley Get

get.summary: List every datasheet in the corpus
get.description:
List the datasheets, ordered by slug.

Returns:
    One summary per unit.

Read a datasheet in full: its profiles, equipment, rules, and options.

Returns:
    The datasheet, its troop-type profile resolved and each printed rule
    name carrying the entry it resolves to.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when no datasheet carries the slug.

post.summary: Cost and equip one block of an army list
post.description:
Size and equip a datasheet, and derive what the block costs.

Says nothing about whether a list of these is legal -- army composition
is not modelled yet. This costs one block and refuses one the datasheet
does not allow. A ``frontage`` re-forms the block that many models wide,
which changes the footprint it stands on and nothing about its cost.

Returns:
    The block, its points and effective loadout derived.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when no datasheet carries the slug; 422, when the
        datasheet does not allow the size or the options asked for.

post.summary: Resolve one round of close combat between two units
post.description:
Deploy two units, fight one round, and score it.

One round: both sides strike in Initiative order, the Wounds tally into a
combat result, and the loser takes its Break test. What a round does not
cover is the rest of the engagement — a pursuit, a second round, and the
Stand & Shoot a charge would be met with, which needs the Movement phase's
charge sequence rather than a charge recorded on the charger.

A side the corpus cannot field is refused before any dice are walked: an
unknown slug is a 404, and a size, option or weapon the datasheet does not
allow is a 422 naming which side asked for it.

Returns:
    The round resolved: each side's casualty distribution and Break-test
    outcomes, who won, and every rule the engine held without applying.

post.summary: Resolve one volley of shooting, and the panic it causes
post.description:
Shoot one unit at another and resolve the panic its casualties cause.

``distance`` is in inches; ``moved`` says the shooter moved this turn.
``battle_strength`` is the target's size at the start of the battle, which
governs the Fall Back or Flee split; it defaults to the size it is shot at.

A side the corpus cannot field is refused before any dice are walked: an
unknown slug is a 404, and a size, option or weapon the datasheet does not
allow is a 422 naming which side asked for it. The shooter must carry
something with a missile profile.

Returns:
    The volley resolved: the scores each roll needs, the wound and casualty
    distributions, what the target's nerve does, and every rule the volley
    holds without applying.

get.summary: List every weapon entry in the corpus
get.description:
List the weapon entries, ordered by slug.

Returns:
    One summary per weapon.

Read a weapon entry in full: its profiles, its rules, its restrictions.

Returns:
    The entry, each profile's printed rule names carrying what they resolve
    to.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when no entry carries the slug.

get.summary: List every armour entry in the corpus
get.description:
List the armour entries, ordered by slug.

An armour entry prints no rules and no long text, so a listing serves each
one whole rather than projecting a summary that could drift from it.

Returns:
    Every entry.

Read one armour entry: its armour value, and what it leaves out.

Returns:
    The entry.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when no entry carries the slug.

get.summary: List every rule entry in the corpus
get.description:
List the rule entries, ordered by slug.

Returns:
    One summary per entry.

get.summary: Report what the corpus prints that the engine never reads
get.description:
Report every gap between the corpus and the engine, with the ledger's reason for each.

Returns:
    The gaps, and the ledger entries no gap needs any more.

Read a rule entry in full: its text, its effects, and what it leaves out.

Returns:
    The rule entry.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when no entry carries the slug. A rule the corpus
        prints without an entry has none to read; ``/coverage``
        names those.

Acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement
Acknowledgement.description:
One gap, known and left open, with why.

``subject`` is how the gap is addressed: the rule's slug for a rule without
effects (one entry covers every place referencing it), ``<unit>/<row>`` for a
profile row, the weapon or armour slug for printed notes, ``<unit>/<option>``
for an option, ``<rule>/<sequence>/<step>`` for an effect needing a step no
program registers yet, for a program's effect no corpus side reaches and for
one its step cannot run, and the mechanic's slug for a mechanic a rule needs.

Address.title: Address
Address.description:
A printed step and the role acting there, optionally narrowed to a block on its path.

``in`` and ``not_in`` name a sequence the step is printed in, or a step
whose block runs it, as a Stand & Shoot volley runs inside stand-and-shoot.

AmountParameter.title: AmountParameter
AmountParameter.description:
An X that is a number, or a dice roll where ``dice`` allows one.

``min`` and ``max`` bound a number. Two sources of one rule sum their X
(``combine``).

Armour.title: Armour
Armour.description: An armour entry: a suit with its own value, or an addition.

ArmourGate.title: ArmourGate
ArmourGate.description: A piece of armour in use, after bars.

AttackGate.title: AttackGate
AttackGate.description: What the attack is, read from the attacking fighter's sources.

BaseSize.title: BaseSize
BaseSize.description: Base footprint of a single model, in millimetres.

Bounded.title: Bounded
Bounded.description: An amount with the printed bound on the value it moves.

Cancels.title: Cancels
Cancels.description: Which effects landing on the canceller's own address are removed.

Characteristic.title: Characteristic
Characteristic.description:
The profile characteristics; values are the printed abbreviations.

The single declaration of the vocabulary: profile rows are keyed by
it, tests match on it, and rule effects will name it.

ChargeArc.title: ChargeArc
ChargeArc.description:
Which arc a charge struck.

The rulebook caps the charge Initiative bonus per arc (front vs flank
or rear), but flank and rear diverge elsewhere — the combat-result
bonuses each grants differ — so all three are distinguished here, and
each arc carries its own printed numbers.

ChargedBy.title: ChargedBy
ChargedBy.description: A charge into the round: who made it, how far it carried, which arc it struck.

Comparison.title: Comparison
Comparison.description: One comparator and the value it compares against.

Coverage.title: Coverage
Coverage.description: The gaps found, ordered by kind then subject, and the ledger entries nothing needs.

Deployment.title: Deployment
Deployment.description: One side put on the table: a datasheet, sized and equipped, weapon in hand.

Effect.title: Effect
Effect.description:
One printed effect.

``of`` names whose characteristic an add or set changes, since a step reads
the characteristics of both models at once.

Entry.title: Entry
Entry.description: The kind of corpus entry a gap occurs in.

FactGate.title: FactGate
FactGate.description: A fact compared against a value.

FactRef.title: FactRef
FactRef.description:
A fact read where the effect lands, relative to the bearer when it belongs to a side.

A fact is a state fact, a step's output named by the step, a derived fact
or a characteristic.

Fight.title: Fight
Fight.description: Two sides meeting in close combat, and the charge that brought them together.

FightReport.title: FightReport
FightReport.description:
One round of close combat, resolved exactly.

The engine works in rationals; these are floats, because JSON has no
other number and a caller plotting a distribution wants one. The exact
values stay reachable from Python.

``first_striker`` names the side Initiative put first, or is ``None`` when
equal Initiative made the blows simultaneous -- a Great Weapon's Strike
Last is why a higher-Initiative unit can still swing second.
``not_modelled`` names the rules the round held without applying, so a
figure is never quietly wrong.

FightSide.title: FightSide
FightSide.description:
One side of a resolved round: what it fielded, what it lost, whether it held.

``casualties`` is the distribution of models this side has lost by the end
of the round -- index ``k`` is the probability it loses exactly ``k`` -- and
``expected_casualties`` its mean, which is the number an averaging
simulator would report and the one the distribution exists to replace.
The three Break-test figures are conditional on nothing: each is the
probability of that outcome *over the whole round*, so they sum to this
side's chance of losing with models left to test, and a side that mostly
wins shows three small numbers.

FoeGate.title: FoeGate
FoeGate.description: The enemy model, by troop type, army or a rule it has.

Footprint.title: Footprint
Footprint.description:
The rectangle a block occupies once it forms up.

The formation it takes, and the table space that costs: ``files`` models
across by ``ranks`` deep, each model on a base of the datasheet's size. A
rear rank standing short still occupies its whole rank, so the depth is the
ranks rather than the models.

Gap.title: Gap
Gap.description:
One gap, where it occurs, and the ledger's reason for it if acknowledged.

``reason`` is None for an unacknowledged gap, which is what fails the gate.

GapKind.title: GapKind
GapKind.description: How a piece of the corpus fails to reach the maths.

Kind.title: Kind
Kind.description:
What a printed name turns out to name.

A caller following a reference needs the route as well as the slug, and the
two cannot be inferred from the name: "Daith's Reaper" is filed both as a
weapon and as the rule that weapon carries.

Limit.title: Limit
Limit.description: How many times an effect may apply over a period.

Muster.title: Muster
Muster.description: What a caller asks to field: a datasheet, a model count, and options by name.

MusteredUnit.title: MusteredUnit
MusteredUnit.description:
A block of an army list: a datasheet sized and equipped, and what it costs.

The view over :class:`~avelorn.tow.muster.Complement`. It carries the
datasheet by slug rather than whole, because a list is read as a list --
a caller wanting the profiles follows ``unit`` to the datasheet route.
``equipment`` and ``special_rules`` are the effective ones, the chosen
options' adds and removes already folded in, so a block says what the
models actually carry rather than what the datasheet offered. ``weapons``
narrows the equipment to the weapons among it, each saying whether it can
be used in close combat -- what a caller naming a weapon chooses from.
``footprint`` is the table space the block takes, at the frontage asked for
or the datasheet's default, which a caller drawing it needs and cannot
derive from a slug.

Operation.title: Operation
Operation.description: What an effect does where it lands.

OptionDetail.title: OptionDetail
OptionDetail.description: One option, the rules it adds and removes resolved.

OptionKind.title: OptionKind
OptionKind.description: Coarse category of a unit option.

OptionScope.title: OptionScope
OptionScope.description: Who takes an option: the whole unit, or models of it.

Panic.title: Panic
Panic.description:
What a volley's casualties do to the target's nerve.

``tests`` is the chance the unit is forced to test at all -- it lost more
than a quarter of the models it started the phase with, and something is
left to test. The four outcomes below it are unconditional and exhaust the
space: a unit that is never forced to test simply ``holds``.

Period.title: Period
Period.description: What a limit counts uses over.

PrintedParameter.title: PrintedParameter
PrintedParameter.description: An X kept as the text its bracket prints: a text-only stub's, read by no effect.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.description:
One row of a characteristic profile, keyed by the printed abbreviations.

A unit may have several rows, e.g. rank-and-file plus champion. The
row is written flat in the printed form ({ name: ..., M: 5, ... });
a validator gathers the abbreviation keys into ``characteristics``,
so the vocabulary is declared once, on :class:`Characteristic`.

``role`` says which part of the model the row describes
(:class:`ProfileRole`). Every row states it.

A mount row lists its own weapons in ``equipment``. The unit's list
holds the other rows' equipment and the mount's armour, such as barding.

ProfileDetail.title: ProfileDetail
ProfileDetail.description: One weapon profile, its rule references resolved.

ProfileRole.title: ProfileRole
ProfileRole.description:
What a profile row is a row *of*.

A datasheet's rows are not alternatives; they are the parts a model is made
of. A Silver Helm prints three: the rider, the champion who replaces one
rider, and the Barded Elven Steed every rider sits on. Reading any one of
them as "the unit's profile" drops the others.

The distinction is not cosmetic. A champion is one model of the unit
fighting at its own line (#46); a mount is carried by *every* model and
fights alongside it, contributing its own attacks and lending the ridden
model its Movement. Which row is which cannot be inferred safely at the
point of use -- a mount is recognisable only by the shape of its dashes --
so it is recorded here, once, when the datasheet is written.

Quantity.title: Quantity
Quantity.description:
A quantity an effect can change, in the rulebook's own modifier vocabulary.

A closed, append-only enum: a member joins when an imported rule needs it.
A profile :class:`~avelorn.tow.schema.unit.Characteristic` is the one
quantity kept apart, a stat vocabulary used far beyond modifiers, so an
operation's key is a Quantity or a Characteristic.

Reference.title: Reference
Reference.description:
A name as an entry prints it, and the entry it resolves to.

``slug`` addresses the entry and ``kind`` says which registry holds it, so a
caller can follow the name without knowing how one finds its file. A rule's
name is the rule's display name with the reference's X substituted.

Both are ``None`` together only for equipment the corpus prints with no
entry behind it; a rule reference always binds, or the corpus fails to load.

RerollOn.title: RerollOn
RerollOn.description: Which dice at the landing a re-roll covers, by result or by natural face.

Role.title: Role
Role.description: Who acts at a step, relative to the model whose rule it is.

Rule.title: Rule
Rule.description:
A rules-page entry (special rule or core rule), text verbatim, with its effects.

``may`` marks a rule its player may decline. ``not_on`` names the profile
rows the rule stops at, as "but not its mount" does. ``needs`` names the
mechanics a printed clause needs that the engine lacks, each a ledger subject.
``notes`` are the author's words on the scope modelled and what is left out.

RuleSummary.title: RuleSummary
RuleSummary.description:
A rule entry as a listing shows it: what it is, and whether it reaches the maths.

``factors`` says whether the entry carries effects; a text-only entry does
not. ``references`` counts the places referencing it -- units, options, troop
types, weapons, and other rules' grants, whatever their X -- so a listing
sorts by what would matter most to model next.

SelectorParameter.title: SelectorParameter
SelectorParameter.description: An X that names one of a closed set, keyed by slug: Hatred's hated enemies.

SelectorValue.title: SelectorValue
SelectorValue.description: One value a selector X may take, and how the bracket prints it.

Site.title: Site
Site.description: Where a gap occurs: an entry, by slug (``<unit>/<option>`` for an option).

Step.title: Step
Step.description:
A printed step.

Ward Saves is printed in the shooting sequence. It is listed under combat
too, since Killing Blow and Cleaving Blow print that Ward saves can be
attempted as normal in combat.

StepSequence.title: StepSequence
StepSequence.description: A printed sequence, by the name an address gives it.

TroopType.title: TroopType
TroopType.description: Closed set from the rulebook's troop-type table.

TroopTypeProfile.title: TroopTypeProfile
TroopTypeProfile.description:
A troop type's rank-and-file data, and how it ranks up.

``models_per_rank`` is how many models a rank must hold to count
toward the Rank Bonus, or None for a troop type that does not rank up
(Swarm, Heavy Chariot, the monsters and war machines that fight as
single models); ``max_rank_bonus`` is the most extra ranks it may
claim. ``unit_strength`` is each model's Unit Strength as the
troop-type table prints it — a fixed count, or "As Starting Wounds"
for the troop types whose strength scales with the model.
``special_rules`` are the rules the troop type confers on every
unit of it (Regular Infantry's Press of Battle, say), as references —
the type's own rules, held apart from the datasheet's
``special_rules`` because their owner is the troop type, not the unit.

UnitDetail.title: UnitDetail
UnitDetail.description:
A datasheet as reading one shows it: the entry, every printed name resolved.

Everything :class:`~avelorn.tow.schema.unit.Unit` prints, except that its
equipment, its special rules and its options' rules arrive as
:class:`Reference`. Resolving on the way out is what keeps a caller from
re-deriving it: a printed name does not become a slug by slugifying it, nor
a reference a name by reading it.

UnitSize.title: UnitSize
UnitSize.description: Allowed model count for a unit.

UnitStrengthMarker.title: UnitStrengthMarker
UnitStrengthMarker.description:
The troop-type table's non-numeric Unit Strength markers.

A closed, append-only vocabulary like the rulebook's other tables: a
member joins when the Unit Strength column prints a new marker in place
of a number. ``STARTING_WOUNDS`` is the table's "W" — the model's Unit
Strength is its starting Wounds, not a fixed count. Each marker names a
distinct resolution, so the troop type must match on the member rather
than lump every non-numeric value together.

UnitSummary.title: UnitSummary
UnitSummary.description:
A datasheet as a listing shows it: what it costs, how it is fielded, who fields it.

``armies`` is every army filing the datasheet, by slug, which a listing
groups by. It is plural because a slug may be filed under several -- a
mount or a beast that more than one army takes -- so a unit belongs to as
many branches of a browser as field it.

Volley.title: Volley
Volley.description: One unit shooting another, and what the shot has to travel through.

VolleyReport.title: VolleyReport
VolleyReport.description:
One volley of shooting, resolved exactly, and what it did to the target's nerve.

Each score is the one the rank and file's roll needed in the volley, with
every rule in force folded in; scores that differ between attacks are joined
with "or", and "-" is a roll not made. ``wounds`` is the distribution of
unsaved wounds and ``casualties`` the models removed; they differ only when
the volley would overkill the unit or its models have more than one Wound.

Volleyed.title: Volleyed
Volleyed.description: A unit in a volley: the one shooting, or the one shot at.

WeaponDetail.title: WeaponDetail
WeaponDetail.description:
A weapon entry as reading one shows it, its rule names resolved per profile.

Per profile rather than pooled, because a weapon with two of them need not
print the same rules on both -- a Brace of Drakefire Pistols carries Quick
Shot when fired and Extra Attacks in close combat.

WeaponMatch.title: WeaponMatch
WeaponMatch.description: A weapon, named by its family or its slug.

WeaponStrength.title: WeaponStrength
WeaponStrength.description:
A weapon profile's Strength, as printed.

Absolute ("4"), or relative to the wielder's own Strength ("S",
"S+2").

WeaponSummary.title: WeaponSummary
WeaponSummary.description:
A weapon as a listing shows it: what it is, and which phase can use it.

``fights`` and ``shoots`` are read off the profiles, because a caller
choosing a weapon for a melee or a volley must not be offered the wrong
half, and guessing from the name would be guessing.

WeaponType.title: WeaponType
WeaponType.description:
A weapon's family in the Weapons of War chapter — a closed, append-only set.

The rulebook groups weapons into families a rule can speak to as one ("any
bow" — a longbow, shortbow, warbow or the Bow of Avelorn). The source does
not carry the family as a field, and the individual weapon entries do not
name it, so it is hand-authored here. A member joins, and a weapon is
classified, only when a rule needs to gate on the family — the same
just-in-time discipline the rest of the vocabulary follows. Values are slugs,
matching the id convention of rules and weapons, so a future rule specific to
a weapon family can key on the family as it keys on a slug.

When.title: When
When.description:
What fires an effect.

The trigger is ``step`` and ``by``. It may also read the ``natural`` face
its die shows, the outcome it ``is``, the score it ``needed`` or the
equipment its option ``holds``. The gates must hold as well.

Wieldable.title: Wieldable
Wieldable.description:
A weapon a block carries, and which phases can put it in hand.

A bow has no Combat profile and a hand weapon no missile one, so a caller
resolving a melee or a volley must not offer the wrong half. The facts
belong here rather than in the caller because they are read off the weapon
entry, and a caller guessing from the name would be guessing.
